title: Hemisphere Finder: Your Quarter of Earth
description: Use the Hemisphere Finder to work out which northern, southern, eastern and western hemispheres any place belongs to — and the rare overlaps. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York is northern and western, Sydney is southern and eastern — and Kiribati is the only country that sits in all four hemispheres at once.
quick_answer: The Hemisphere Finder tells you which hemispheres any place on Earth belongs to — northern or southern by the equator, eastern or western by the prime meridian. Enter a location or coordinates and read its quarter of the globe, with the edge cases explained.
steps_intro: Every point on Earth has a hemisphere address with four possible labels:

body.t: Worksheets ask 'which hemisphere is Brazil in?' and the honest answer is three of them. Tools like this turn a trick question into a real lesson. Check the boundary lines with the
Southern hemisphere means flipped seasons — Sydney's December is summer. Checking hemispheres before booking explains weather expectations better than any brochure.
A sign error in latitude or longitude flips a hemisphere. If a dataset claims a point is in the northern hemisphere but plots off Perth, the finder exposes the mistake.
Which country spans all four hemispheres? Only Kiribati. Which continent sits in all four? Africa. These make the abstract grid memorable.

examples.label: Example · Brazil breaks the simple answer

body.t: Brazil is mostly southern and entirely western — but its northern states cross the equator, so the country spans northern, southern and western hemispheres at once. Most large countries refuse a single label.

examples.label: Example · The point in all four

body.t: Only one spot is in all four hemispheres simultaneously: 0°, 0° in the Gulf of Guinea, where the equator and prime meridian cross — open ocean, marked by a weather buoy, not a monument.

rows: Both — the prime meridian crosses it
popular_table.note: East/west follows the common convention: eastern hemisphere runs 0° to 180°E, western 0° to 180°W. Some textbooks draw the divide at 20°W and 160°E to keep continents whole — a convention, not a law.

faq: Northern/southern split at the equator (0° latitude); eastern/western split at the prime meridian (0° longitude) and the 180° meridian on the far side. Latitude sign gives the first pair, longitude sign the second.
Which country is in all four hemispheres?

Kiribati. Its islands stretch across the equator and across the 180° meridian region of the Pacific, giving it territory in the northern, southern, eastern and western hemispheres — a distinction no other nation holds.
Which continent is in all four?
Africa. It crosses the equator and the prime meridian (through Ghana, near Accra — only about 21 km of parallel arc from Greenwich's line), and extends past both divides.
Is most of Earth's land in one hemisphere?
Yes — the northern hemisphere holds roughly two thirds of all land, which is why 'winter' in December describes most of the world's population but not most of its surface.
What hemisphere is the UK in?
Northern, and split on east/west: the prime meridian runs through Greenwich, so Britain has ground in both the eastern and western hemispheres within the same city — London straddles the line.
North/south does — the seasons are six months out of phase across the equator. East/west changes only clock time, not season.
Where do the hemispheres all meet?
At two points: 0°, 0° in the Gulf of Guinea (all four meet) and 0°, 180° in the Pacific. The poles belong to every longitude's hemisphere argument and settle none.
